summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned his MA and PhD, and later served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen. His posts include Associate Professor at McMaster University and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Shechen Gyaltsab (1871–1926) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (b. 1966) is an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held an academic post at Cornell University from circa 1978 to 1998 and became a professor at Harvard University circa 1998.

Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Dudjom Rinpoche, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau. He was a professor at Renmin University of China and served on an Academic Advisory Board at Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, A. K. Ramanujan, and D. R. Nagaraj. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, University of Chicago, and Columbia University.

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University under mentors including Dongchu and Lingyuan. He held positions at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Shenghai Li works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Li completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., having also studied with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Ram Shankar Tripathi, among others.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, as well as under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu, among others. He taught at Dzogchen Monastery and became the first khenpo of the new shedra at Dzongsar Monastery.

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries under teachers including Gung Tang Lodrö Gyatso. He served as Dean at the Buddhist Academy of China and President of the Buddhist Association.

Sherry B. Ortner is an anthropologist in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Los Angeles.
Sherry Chayat is active in the field of Buddhist studies. She studied at Vassar College from circa 1961 to 1965 and trained under traditional teacher Eido Shimano from circa 1967 to 1998.

Shi Hu (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Cornell University and Columbia University under John Dewey, later holding posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica.

Shichang Ma (1934–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He worked as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy from 1963 to 1978 and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.

Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1925 to 1928 and later held an academic post there from circa 1931 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His academic appointments include serving as an assistant at Kyoto University, an associate professor at Shuchiin University, and an associate professor at Shitennoji University.

Shigeki Moro works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai Universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, holding posts at Hanazono University and Waseda University.

Shigemasa Fukui is a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1954 to 1963 and later served as a professor at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 2006.
